UserAccount.title: UserAccount
UserAccount.description: Represents a user account within the Petediano Pro application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account.

profilePictureUrl.description: URL of the user's profile picture.

signUpDate.description: Date and time when the user created their account.

lastLogin.description: Date and time of the user's last login.

vipStatus.description: Indicates if the user has VIP status.

GeneratedContent.title: GeneratedContent
GeneratedContent.description: Represents content generated by the AI within the Petediano Pro application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the generated content.

contentType.description: Type of generated content (e.g., motivational quote, funny story, image).

contentUrl.description: URL where the generated content is stored (e.g., image URL, PDF URL).

creationDate.description: Date and time when the content was generated.

likes.description: Number of likes received for the content.

dislikes.description: Number of dislikes received for the content.

comments.description: Comments associated with the generated content.

UserSetting.title: UserSetting
UserSetting.description: Represents user-specific settings for the Petediano Pro application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user settings.

theme.description: User's chosen theme for the app.

font.description: User's preferred font for the app.

notificationPreferences.description: Preferences for notifications, such as on/off.

DeviceData.title: DeviceData
DeviceData.description: Stores information about the device used to access the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the device data.

lastAccessTime.description: Date and time of the last access from this device.

location.description: The most recently recorded location of the device

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, clarity, and scalability for the Petediano Pro application. It leverages structural segregation and consistent access modeling. User-owned data is organized under the `/users/{userId}` path, ensuring clear ownership and simplified security rules.  Collections like `generated_content`, `user_settings`, and `device_data` are created as subcollections of the `/users/{userId}` collection, and are used to store resources related to user. This approach ensures that all documents within these subcollections inherit the same security posture, and that rules are not filters. The design avoids `get()` calls in security rules by storing all access control information directly within the relevant documents, achieving authorization independence.

The structure supports required QAPs (Queries and Presentations) through:

1.  **Secure Lists:** By segregating data based on ownership (`/users/{userId}/generated_content`) and using path-based rules, list operations are inherently secured as they only return content owned by the authenticated user.
2.  **No Rules as Filters:** The structure avoids combining data with different access requirements in the same collection.  Each collection has a uniform security posture.

The schema employs explicit state modeling (e.g., `vipStatus` in `UserAccount`). It maintains radical consistency through semantic naming conventions (e.g., `userAccountId`). This ensures that the data is easily understood and maintained.
